name: ramp-width-select-widen
description: #1298: ramp width is a player choice and a built ramp can be selected and widened. A player arms the ramp tool, raises the width param from the default 3 to 5 with the width stepper, drags the corridor and confirms (cost scales with width); once the ramp is dug BuiltRamp state reports one ramp of width 5. The player then clicks the ramp in the scene: the selection bar offers Widen and no Demolish (a ramp is a terrain feature, not a building). Clicking Widen orders only the delta, and once the extra side strips are dug the ramp is 7 wide. Contract for console-api state: builtRampCount (state.builtRamps.length) and builtRampWidth (width of the first built ramp, 0 when none).

steps.description: Staffed vehicles come unmanned (#551) - crew rock_digger #3 with driver #4 before ordering excavation work. Same bootstrap as building-ramp-visual.json.

steps.command: build_ramp origin:20,20 direction:south length:11 depth:6 width:5
steps.description: Player arms the ramp tool, sets depth 6 and raises the width param to 5 via its stepper (data-field="width" on the ParamStrip, steps through RAMP_WIDTH_OPTIONS), drags the 11-tile corridor and confirms. The charged cost reflects width 5 (length * 5 * RAMP_COST_PER_METER_PER_WIDTH).

expect.note: Order charged and queued; nothing is built yet. Exact cost is asserted by unit tests; the player-visible claim here is that a click-driven order at width 5 lands.

steps.description: Wait for every dig_ramp_segment to land; the finished ramp is recorded as a BuiltRamp. Condition-based wait on builtRampCount, never a tick pad.

Player clicks the dug ramp in the scene (viewport centre after a near top-down focusTile on the corridor midpoint, so the ray lands on the floor tile whatever the dug depth). The selection bar shows the ramp with a Widen action; Demolish must not exist (a ramp is a terrain feature).

expect.note: Ramp selected; widen offered (width 5 < max 7). Demolish absence is asserted by unit tests.

steps.description: Player clicks Widen on the selection bar. Each click steps to the next option (5 -> 7) and orders only the delta cost, length * (7 - 5) * RAMP_COST_PER_METER_PER_WIDTH.

expect.note: Order placed and charged; the ramp is still 5 wide until the last new strip segment is dug. The exact delta is asserted by unit tests (a float figure, so not pinned here).

steps.description: Wait for the side strips to be dug; the built ramp then reports width 7.
